summary: Deep pass keeps the first-pass direction (Missouri side, game under) but tightens it. Changes: (1) the side moves from Missouri +5 to Missouri +5.5, the half point better at a slightly higher fair price, because SP+ rates this close to a pick'em (Predictem: Ole Miss favored by under 0.5 at home), while the market says 5.5; (2) 1H Under 35.5 is added as the leg most likely to win. The 1H main line is 30.5, and the forecast (NWS: sunny, 65F, NNE wind about 15 mph, gusts near 20) plus Missouri's run-heavy, clock-draining plan make a 36+ point first half unlikely; (3) corrected record context: Missouri's one loss was 31-24 at Mississippi State (Sep 26), its 8th straight loss to a ranked SEC team, and that tempers the Missouri case. Ole Miss's one loss was 52-28 at Florida, where Florida ran for 302 yards. Both QBs are healthy (Simmons is off the report) and Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy is out. Missouri's havoc defense (4th nationally, 3 sacks per game) meets an Ole Miss OL that allows about 1 sack per game and an offense that has scored on 20 of 20 red-zone trips, so the edges are modest. No player props (Ohio).

legs.note: This is the leg most likely to win. The 1H main line is 30.5, and 35.5 needs both teams near 18 first-half points. NNE wind of 15 mph with gusts near 20 (NWS, 247Sports, Covers) hurts downfield passing. Drinkwitz wants long Roberts drives (34 carries vs Texas A&M), and Missouri's defense ranks 4th in havoc. The risk is Ole Miss's 38.8 ppg offense and its 20-of-20 red-zone scoring, and that Florida put up 52 on this Ole Miss defense.

This is the strongest edge. SP+ sees about a pick'em, and Missouri ranks 5th in net adjusted EPA per play, while Ole Miss's defense ranks about 91st in success rate and about 100th in adjusted EPA. The line moved from -6 to -5/-5.5 toward Missouri. Experts lean Missouri: SBR, SportsGambler, TheRx, Predictem, SI (ML), Bleacher Nation (ML) and VegasInsider, against Covers and Lineups.com for Ole Miss. The case is weakened by Missouri's 8-game losing streak against ranked SEC teams, a sold-out homecoming crowd and Hardy being out. Missouri has covered 5 of its last 6 at +5.5 (SportsGambler).

SportsLine's 10,000-simulation model projects 57 points (Under about 53%). SBR, TheRx and Covers take the under, while Bleacher Nation and LVSB take the over. Missouri is 4-1 to the under in its last 5, and the under is 8-2 in Ole Miss's last 10 games as a home favorite. Wind and Missouri's possession-length plan help the under. Against it, the teams average 38.8 and 35.8 ppg, and Ole Miss's defense ranks 123rd on third down.

Ole Miss has allowed 140+ rushing yards in at least 4 straight games, 302 of them to Florida, and allows 28 ppg (108th-109th). Roberts leads the SEC with 828 yds and ran for 222 last week. Simmons has 14 TD and 1 INT, and Missouri ranks 29th in EPA per dropback. Missouri's run efficiency ranks poorly (75th-83rd in offensive success rate), and Hardy is out. The -125 price is already about 52% fair.

legs.desc: Ole Miss Rebels team total Under 31.5
legs.note: Missouri allows 16.6 ppg and 2.3 YPC (4th), and allows opponents 32.3% on third down. Wind limits Chambliss downfield, and Missouri's ball control limits Ole Miss's possessions. Against the under, Ole Miss allows only about 1 sack per game (1st in SEC) and has scored on all 20 red-zone trips (18 TD). Lean only.

research:
1. QBs/personnel: Austin Simmons (MIZ) went 45/75 (60%), 744 yds, 4 TD, 5 INT, 147.6 rating at Ole Miss in 2025 (hurt in Week 2) and was Jaxson Dart's backup in 2024 (32 attempts). In 2026 at Missouri he has 1,434 yds, 14 TD, 1 INT in 6 games (17/19, 4 TD in the opener; 340 yds vs Florida) (FieldLevel, StatSniper, TheRebelWalk). Trinidad Chambliss (OM) went 3,279 yds, 31 TD, 7 INT at Ferris State (D-II) from 2021-24. In 2025 at Ole Miss he went 66%, 3,937 yds, 22 TD, 3 INT plus 527 rush yds and won SEC Newcomer of the Year. In 2026 he is at 70.1%, 1,435 yds, 11 TD, 4 INT with an 82.4 QBR (about 15th) (WalterFootball, Wikipedia, TheRebelWalk). OM's backup is former 5-star Deuce Knight (2 career appearances). Skill players: Jamal Roberts (MIZ) leads the SEC with 828 yds (222 on 34 carries vs Texas A&M), Cayden Lee has 42 catches for 616 yds and 5 TD, and OM RB Kewan Lacy is back from a shoulder injury on a rotation (39 yds vs Vandy).
2. Injuries (Fri SEC report via TheRebelWalk, HottyToddy, Rotowire, 247): Simmons is off the report and available. MIZ: RB Ahmad Hardy out, Lee probable, LB Beasley and TE Norfleet questionable but trending toward playing, and Woodyard and Webb trending toward playing (24 players were on the Wednesday list). OM: S Edwin Joseph out (ankle surgery, multiple games), S MJ Preston questionable (downgraded Fri), and DB Nascar McCoy lost, which thins the secondary.
3. Advanced: Predictem says SP+ has MIZ a few spots above OM, with OM's offense top-10 and OM's defense outside the top 50. MIZ defense: 4th in havoc (22.8%), 5th in net adjusted EPA, 14th in success rate, 3.0 sacks per game (13th). MIZ offense: 55th in adjusted EPA, 75th-83rd in success rate, 29th in EPA per dropback. OM defense: about 91st in success rate, about 100th in adjusted EPA, 45.9% allowed on third down (123rd) (Rock M Nation, VegasInsider and other previews). OM offense: 38.8 ppg, 433.8 ypg, 43.9% on third down, 20/20 red-zone scoring (18 TD). MIZ: 35.8 ppg, 438 ypg, allows 16.6 ppg and 32.3% on third down. I found no pace data.
4. Scheme: Roberts and Missouri's gap run game face an OM front that has allowed 140+ rushing yards in 4 straight games and 302 at Florida (53 carries, 1 TFL, 0 sacks). OM's pass-first offense (about 300 pass ypg) and its OL (about 1 sack allowed per game, 1st in SEC) face Missouri's havoc front. OM's thinned safety group faces Simmons and Lee.
5. Coaching: Pete Golding is in his first full year (former Saban DC). The OC is John David Baker and the DC is Bryan Brown. Golding's halftime challenge failed at Florida. Drinkwitz: 19-17-1 ATS as an underdog, 7-12 ATS as a road dog, 10-17 in true road games, 33-5 vs lower-SP+ teams, and 8 straight losses to ranked SEC teams (SI, Roundtable, NBC).
6. Situational: OM homecoming, sold out, 2:30 CT on SEC Network. No bye for either team. Simmons and Lee return to face their former team, which adds revenge and emotion. MIZ is coming off a 27-6 home win over Texas A&M, and OM off a 52-17 road win at Vanderbilt.
7. Results and history: MIZ beat UAPB 54-14 and Kansas, lost 24-31 at Mississippi State, beat Florida 45-17 and beat Texas A&M 27-6. OM beat Louisville 41-38, Charlotte 41-9 and LSU, lost 28-52 at Florida and beat Vanderbilt 52-17. Missouri leads the series 7-1, OM's last win came in 1974, and the last meeting was a 38-27 MIZ win at Faurot. ATS: MIZ 3-3 (3-3 O/U) and OM 2-3 (3-2 O/U). Underdogs have covered 4 of OM's last 5 home games, and the under is 8-2 in OM's last 10 as a home favorite (Covers, SportsChatPlace).
8. Weather: NWS (updated 10/16) has Saturday partly sunny becoming sunny, high near 65F, NNE wind around 15 mph. 247Sports has NNE 10-15. Covers cites gusts near 20 mph and no rain, a slight downfield-passing drag.
9. Experts/models: SportsLine model, Under 58.5 (projects 57; a second version says Over, conflicting). SBR: MIZ +5.5 and Under. SportsGambler: MIZ +5.5. TheRx: MIZ +5.5 and Under. Predictem: MIZ +6. SportsBettingReport: MIZ 31-27 and Under. SI: MIZ ML +180. Bleacher Nation: MIZ ML and Over. VegasInsider: MIZ ML. Sports Gambling Podcast: 2 of 3 on MIZ +6.5. Covers: OM ML and Under (wind). Lineups.com: OM -5.5 (34-28). LVSB: OM -5 and Over. Consensus is MIZ on the spread, with the total leaning under. Line: OM opened -6 (OM -6.5 on Mon at some books), now -5.5 (-5 at BetMGM). The total was steady at 58.5. ML about OM -196 to -225 and MIZ +162 to +185. I found no public betting splits.
